summary: Local PDF parser that turns PDFs into Markdown, JSON with bounding boxes or HTML for RAG, and can auto-tag PDFs for accessibility.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenDataLoader PDF extracts content from PDFs into Markdown, JSON (with a bounding box and type for every element) and HTML, ready for LLM and RAG pipelines. It keeps reading order on multi-column pages, and a hybrid mode sends hard pages such as complex tables, scans, formulas and charts to a local AI backend. It can also auto-tag PDFs to Tagged PDF as a step toward accessibility.
sixtySeconds.problem: Feeding PDFs to an LLM usually loses tables, headings and reading order. This gives clean, structured output while running entirely on your machine.
whoFor: Teams handling legal, health or finance documents locally
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for fast, local, deterministic parsing with element positions, plus an optional hybrid mode for tough documents and SDKs for Python, Node.js and Java.

overview: Install the Python package, then call convert with a list of files or folders, an output folder and formats such as markdown and json. Batch files in one call, since each call starts a Java process.

Fast mode is the default and needs no server. For complex tables, scanned PDFs (OCR), formulas or chart descriptions, install the hybrid extra, start opendataloader-pdf-hybrid in one terminal and run the client with --hybrid docling-fast in another.
Everything runs locally with no data sent to the cloud. It includes prompt-injection filtering and a LangChain integration. The core is Apache 2.0; PDF/UA export is an enterprise add-on.
